flows:
Navigate to http://localhost:8080/ then For every product card on the page, read its name and its stock or scarcity message (for example "Only 3 left" or "12 in stock").
Store them all as one text in the form "name: message | name: message" as stock_1.
Navigate to http://localhost:8080/ again so the page fully loads fresh, read every product card again the same way, and store the list as stock_2.
Navigate to http://localhost:8080/ once more and store the list as stock_3.
Read each list from the page after its own fresh load; do not copy an earlier value.
Do not add anything to the cart.
If there are no stock messages, @v16:"store \"none\" for all three".
Never enter payment details and never place a real order.

summary:
The page loaded successfully and visibly shows a stock message on each product card, but the extraction check relied on readable anchors rather than reading the text within each card. That made the test stop before collecting the first list.
Update the extraction to locate each product card and read its name and stock-message text from the card itself, without requiring an anchor. Then reload and repeat the reading separately for all three lists.
one_liner: The automation could not identify the visible stock messages because its locator expected readable anchors that this page does not provide.
reason: The required starting extraction failed because stock-message elements have no readable anchors.
